nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. If terms $f$ and $g$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in a context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$ (they have the same denotation in every environment), and terms $a$ and $b$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$, then the applications $f\,a$ and $g\,b$ are semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Semantic equality is a congruence for application

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and every term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the redex $(\lambda.\,t)\,a$ is semantically equal in $I$ (has the same denotation in every environment) to the instantiation $t[a]$, which replaces the newest free variable of $t$ by $a$.
nodes.title: Beta is sound for the denotational semantics

nodes.summary: For every term $b$ of type $B$ in the variable context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and every term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the application $(\lambda.\,b)\,a$ is model-equal to $b[a]$, the result of substituting $a$ for the newest variable of $b$.
nodes.title: Model-independent beta equality

nodes.summary: Let $E_1$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in context $\Delta$, $E_2$ one with hole of type $B$ in $\Delta$ producing type $C$ in $\Theta$, and $E_3$ one with hole of type $C$ in $\Theta$ producing type $D$ in $\Xi$. Then $(E_3 \circ E_2) \circ E_1 = E_3 \circ (E_2 \circ E_1)$.
nodes.title: Associativity of composition of STLC contexts

nodes.summary: Let $E_2$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $B$ in variable context $\Delta$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Theta$, and let $E_1$ be one whose hole has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in $\Delta$. The composite $E_2 \circ E_1$, with hole of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ and result of type $C$ in $\Theta$, replaces the hole of $E_2$ by $E_1$; by recursion…
nodes.title: Composition of STLC contexts

nodes.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ of the base types, a value $a$ in the denotation of a type $A$ and an environment $\eta$ for a context $\Gamma$, the extended environment for the context $A :: \Gamma$ sends the newest variable to $a$ and the successor $\mathrm{succ}\,x$ of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(x)$.
nodes.title: Extending a semantic environment in STLC

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $B$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Delta$. For every term $b$ of type $B$ in $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and every term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the term $E[(\lambda.\,b)\,a]$ is model-equal to $E[b[a]]$, where $b[a]$ is the result of substituting $a$ for the newest variable of $b$.
nodes.title: Beta equality inside an STLC context

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A \Rightarrow B$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Delta$. For every term $f$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in $\Gamma$, the term $E[\lambda.\,(f^{\uparrow}\,x_0)]$ is model-equal to $E[f]$, where $f^{\uparrow}$ is $f$ weakened by a newest variable of type $A$ and $x_0$ is that variable.
nodes.title: Eta equality inside an STLC context

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in context $\Delta$. If two terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ are model-equal, then $E[t]$ and $E[u]$ are model-equal.
nodes.title: Model equality is a congruence for STLC contexts

nodes.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ of the base types, the denotation of a well-typed term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ in an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ is the element of the denotation of $A$ defined by recursion on $t$: a variable $x$ denotes $\eta(x)$, an application $f\,a$ denotes the denotation of $f$ applied to the denotation of $a$ (both in $\eta$), and an abstraction $\lambda.\,b$ denotes the function…
nodes.title: Denotation of an STLC term

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to $t'$ in zero or more steps of call-by-value reduction, then $t$ and $t'$ have the same denotation in every environment $\eta$ for their context.
nodes.title: Multi-step reduction preserves STLC denotation

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ evaluates to $v$ under call-by-value big-step evaluation, then $t$ and $v$ have the same denotation in every environment $\eta$ for their context.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation preserves STLC denotation

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one step of call-by-value reduction, then $t$ and $t'$ have the same denotation in every environment $\eta$ for their context.
nodes.title: One reduction step preserves STLC denotation

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $b$ of type $B$ in context $A :: \Gamma$, every term $a$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, the denotation in $\eta$ of $b$ with its newest variable replaced by $a$ equals the denotation of $b$ in the environment that extends $\eta$ by the denotation of $a$ in $\eta$ for the newest variable.
nodes.title: Denotation of an instantiated STLC body

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every type-preserving renaming $\rho$ from context $\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$, every term $t$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the denotation in $\eta$ of the term obtained by renaming the variables of $t$ along $\rho$ equals the denotation of $t$ in the environment that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(\rho(x))$.
nodes.title: Renaming lemma for STLC denotation

nodes.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ of the base types, a type-preserving substitution $\sigma$ mapping each variable of a context $\Gamma$ to a term in a context $\Delta$, and an environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, this is the environment for $\Gamma$ that sends each variable $x$ to the denotation of $\sigma(x)$ in $\eta$.
nodes.title: Denotation of an STLC substitution

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every type-preserving substitution $\sigma$ mapping each variable of a context $\Gamma$ to a term in a context $\Delta$, every term $t$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the denotation in $\eta$ of $t$ with $\sigma$ applied simultaneously to its variables equals the denotation of $t$ in the environment that sends each variable $x$ of…
nodes.title: Substitution lemma for STLC denotation

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, every type $B$, every value $a$ in the denotation of $B$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, the weakening of $t$ to the context $B :: \Gamma$ has, in the environment that extends $\eta$ by $a$ for the newest variable, the same denotation as $t$ in $\eta$.
nodes.title: Weakening preserves STLC denotation

nodes.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ assigning a type $I(b)$ to each base type $b$, the denotation $[\![A]\!]_I$ of a simple type $A$ is defined by recursion on $A$: a base type $b$ denotes $I(b)$, and a function type $A \Rightarrow B$ denotes the type of all functions from $[\![A]\!]_I$ to $[\![B]\!]_I$.
nodes.title: Denotation of simple types

nodes.summary: Given an interpretation $I$ assigning a type to each base type and a typing context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types), an environment for $\Gamma$ assigns to every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, of any simple type $A$, an element of the denotation $[\![A]\!]_I$.
nodes.title: Semantic environments for the denotational semantics of STLC

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every context $\Gamma$ and every type $A$, semantic equality in $I$ of terms of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ (having the same denotation in every environment) is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
nodes.title: Semantic equality is an equivalence relation

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and every term $f$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in a context $\Gamma$, let $f'$ be the weakening of $f$ to the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable $x$ of type $A$. Then the term $\lambda x.\, f'\,x$, which binds $x$, is semantically equal to $f$ in $I$ (has the same denotation in every environment).
nodes.title: Eta is sound for the denotational semantics

nodes.summary: For every term $f$ of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in variable context $\Gamma$, the term $\lambda.\,(f^{\uparrow}\,x_0)$ is model-equal to $f$, where $f^{\uparrow}$ is $f$ weakened by a newest variable of type $A$ and $x_0$ is that variable.
nodes.title: Model-independent eta equality

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. If two terms of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ are semantically equal in $I$ (they have the same denotation in every environment), then their lambda abstractions, terms of type $A \Rightarrow B$ in $\Gamma$, are semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Semantic equality is a congruence for lambda abstraction

nodes.summary: Two terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ are model-equal when, for every interpretation $I$ of the base types by types in the same universe as the type of base types, they are semantically equal in $I$: with function types interpreted as full function spaces, the denotations of $t$ and $u$ agree at every semantic environment for $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Model equality of STLC terms

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to a term $u$ in one call-by-value evaluation step, then $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$: they have the same denotation in every environment.
nodes.title: Single-step evaluation is a semantic equation

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if a term $t$ reduces to a term $u$ in zero or more call-by-value evaluation steps, then $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$: they have the same denotation in every environment.
nodes.title: Multi-step evaluation is a semantic equation

nodes.summary: Let $E_2$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $B$ in variable context $\Delta$ and which produces a term of type $C$ in context $\Theta$, and let $E_1$ be one whose hole has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in $\Delta$. Then for every term $t$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, $(E_2 \circ E_1)[t] = E_2[E_1[t]]$.
nodes.title: Plugging into a composite STLC context

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a typed one-hole context whose hole has type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in variable context $\Delta$. For a term $t$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the plugged term $E[t]$ of type $B$ in $\Delta$ is defined by recursion on $E$: $[\,][t] = t$, $(E\,a)[t] = E[t]\,a$, $(f\,E)[t] = f\,E[t]$ and $(\lambda.\,E)[t] = \lambda.\,E[t]$, where $[\,]$ is the bare hole, $E\,a$…
nodes.title: Plugging a term into an STLC context

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and every simultaneous substitution $\sigma$ that replaces each variable of a context $\Gamma$ by a term of the same type in a context $\Delta$, $\sigma$ is pointwise semantically equal to itself in $I$: for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, the term $\sigma(x)$ has the same denotation as itself in every environment for $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Pointwise semantic equality of substitutions is reflexive

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ is semantically equal to itself in $I$: it has the same denotation as itself in every environment.
nodes.title: Semantic equality is reflexive

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. If terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$ (they have the same denotation in every environment), then for every type-preserving renaming $\rho$ of the variables of $\Gamma$ into a context $\Delta$, the renamed terms $\rho(t)$ and $\rho(u)$ are semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Renaming preserves semantic equality

nodes.summary: Given a renaming $\rho$ from context $\Gamma$ to context $\Delta$ (a type-preserving map from the variables of $\Gamma$ to those of $\Delta$) and an environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the renamed environment for $\Gamma$ sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(\rho(x))$; that is, it is the composite $\eta \circ \rho$.
nodes.title: Renaming an environment

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types as types. Two terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type $A$ in the same context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$ when, for every semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, the denotation of $t$ in $I$ at $\eta$ equals the denotation of $u$ in $I$ at $\eta$.
nodes.title: Semantic equality of terms in a model

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. Let $t$ and $u$ be terms of type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$ that denote the same value in $I$ under every semantic environment. Then for every typed one-hole context $C$ whose hole has type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and which produces a term of type $B$ in context $\Delta$, the terms $C[t]$ and $C[u]$ obtained by plugging $t$ and $u$ into the hole also denote the…
nodes.title: Semantic equality is a congruence for typed contexts

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types as types. Two simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$ when, for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ (of any type) and every semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Delta$, the denotation of the term $\sigma(x)$ in $I$ at $\eta$ equals the denotation of the term $\tau(x)$ in $I$ at $\eta$.
nodes.title: Pointwise semantic equality of substitutions

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, and all simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$ from $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ that are pointwise semantically equal in $I$, the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and the result of applying $\tau$ to $t$ are semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Semantically equal substitutions give semantically equal results

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, if two terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ are semantically equal in $I$, then for every simultaneous substitution $\sigma$ from $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and the result of applying $\sigma$ to $u$ are semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Substitution preserves semantic equality

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, if $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$, then $\tau$ and $\sigma$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of pointwise semantic equality of substitutions

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type in the same context, if $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$, then $u$ and $t$ are semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of semantic equality of terms

nodes.summary: Fix simple types over a type of base types. A one-hole context whose hole has type $A$ in variable context $\Gamma$, and which produces a term of type $B$ in variable context $\Delta$, is built by four rules. The hole itself is such a context, with $\Delta = \Gamma$ and $B = A$. If $C$ produces type $S \Rightarrow T$ in $\Delta$ and $a$ is a term of type $S$ in $\Delta$, then the application $C\,a$ produces type…
nodes.title: Typed one-hole contexts

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all simultaneous substitutions $\sigma$, $\tau$ and $\upsilon$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, if $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$ and $\tau$ and $\upsilon$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$, then $\sigma$ and $\upsilon$ are pointwise semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of pointwise semantic equality of substitutions

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and all terms $t$, $u$ and $w$ of the same type in the same context, if $t$ and $u$ are semantically equal in $I$ and $u$ and $w$ are semantically equal in $I$, then $t$ and $w$ are semantically equal in $I$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of semantic equality of terms

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
